subject: Reliability & SLO follow-up — competitive evaluation vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Reliability & SLO follow-up — competitive evaluation vs hyperscalers

Hi Alex / Emily,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to hear more about NimbusAI's inference footprint and the reliability concerns you're tracking. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: validate that Redwood's serving behaviors (uptime, rate limits, error budgets, failover) meet Nimbus's production SLOs and compare head-to-head with your current hyperscaler endpoints.
- Questions we raised on the call: typical 95th/99th latency targets, burst traffic patterns, and how you expect graceful degradation to behave under partial regional failures.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll run a set of reliability tests (steady-state + burst, multi-region failover sim) against Redwood and a hyperscaler endpoint you nominate.
2) We'll share a short SLO mapping doc and a test plan by EOD tomorrow.
3) You confirm which hyperscaler endpoint & test account we should use, and a list of sample workloads (payload sizes, concurrency profiles).

I've looped in Marissa who will own the SLO mapping and test artifacts and Aditya for engineering coordination.

Attachments: redwood-reliability-slo-sheet.xlsx (SLO mapping template)

Thanks — talk soon,
Ben
--
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0173
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@hyperscale.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Ross <emily.ross@nimbusai.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reliability & SLO follow-up — competitive evaluation vs hyperscalers

Thanks Ben — appreciate the concise recap. A couple clarifications: 

- For the hyperscaler baseline, use our current managed endpoint on GCP (endpoint-id: nimbus-prod-eu). We'll provide a short-lived test key.
- 95th/99th latency targets: 95th < 200ms, 99th < 400ms for single-shot generation; bursts can reach 800 RPS for short windows (1-3 min).
- Error behavior: we expect graceful degradation (queueing/backpressure) rather than outright failures; if you can show how Redwood falls back to a cheaper variant or region, that's ideal.

Emily will send the test key and a minimal payload set by EOD. Please include a simple script we can reuse to run the tests (k6 or locust).

On the failover test: if you can simulate a regional outage and demonstrate traffic shifting and what clients observe (error rates, latency spikes, 429s) that will cover what our ops team cares about.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Johnson
SRE, Hyperscale Research Group
alex.johnson@hyperscale.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@hyperscale.ai>, Emily Ross <emily.ross@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reliability & SLO follow-up — competitive evaluation vs hyperscalers

Hi Alex / Emily — attaching the SLO mapping + test plan as discussed. High-level notes below, pulled from our runbook: 

- Uptime: Redwood-hosted API SLA 99.95% for prod clusters (we'll provide per-route availability numbers during testing).
- Rate limits: Default rate limit is per-project; we can mirror your burst profile. We can also provision a dedicated pool for the POC to remove shared throttles.
- Error budget handling: We expose token-level error breakdowns and will surface 429/5xx counts per test window. We also support automatic fallback policies to model variants and cross-region routing.
- Failover behavior: Our routing can shift to a warm standby region within 45-90s depending on KV cache warmup; during failover you may see transient 5xx spikes and increased tail latencies — we'll capture timelines in traces.

Attached: redwood-reliability-slo-sheet.xlsx (populated); slo-comparison-chart.png (high-level diff vs common hyperscaler configs); redwood-failover-runbook.pdf (short).

Planned deliverables for the POC:
- Test harness (k6 script), workload definitions, and a runbook for failover simulation.
- Post-test report: latency percentiles, error budgets consumed, timeline of failover events, and RPS/throughput curves.

If that aligns, we'll schedule the run next Tue (2026-04-20) unless you prefer earlier.

Thanks,
Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Reliability
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@hyperscale.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Reliability & SLO follow-up — competitive evaluation vs hyperscalers

Quick note from engineering: we'll provision an isolated Redwood Dedicated pool for the POC to ensure no noisy-neighbor throttling. Test account details and the k6 script will be in a shared drive link (I'll DM the link once it's generated).

Two small asks for your test key:
- Please provide an API key that scopes to a single project and has consistent regional routing so we can reproduce the scenario.
- Share a short sample of your payload size distribution (typical prompt lengths and response token counts).

We'll capture traces and upload to the report so you can correlate spikes to infra events.

- Aditya
